scope: Curate distinct image-backed concepts from the final Genesis 1 encode; no film, project or renderer changes.

source.projectManifestNote: Current manifest supplied section identity and boundaries; the exact sampled video is identified independently by SHA256.

reviewMethod.overview: Decoded the complete source using ffmpeg fps=1/5 and scaled to 384x216; opened all three overview sheets (61 images, approximately 2.5 through 302.5 seconds). These uniformly spaced samples were used only to find candidate passages.
reviewMethod.overviewTimestampPrecision: Overview labels are nominal sample-bin centers; source frame time may differ by one 30fps frame. Final card timestamps are explicit ffmpeg seek times.
reviewMethod.finalEvidence: Created both cards using capture-reference with six frames each, then opened each resulting contact sheet before setting observed.
assessmentLimits: Sparse decoded still sequences support relationships and state progression only.
No continuous-playback, motion-smoothness, musical-pacing or audio-sync claim is made.
No user approval of these extracted treatments was inferred.

newReferences.novelty: A gradually drawn enclosure shows container/content semantics with intact type; unlike particle assembly, landscape type or a word becoming material.
Two opposed words acquire a shared fulcrum and differential height; unlike simply pulling words apart or adding emotional weight to one word.

notAdded.reason: Already covered by internal-genesis1-whale-word-composite. The final encode hash differs from the older reference source; the existing card was preserved and no duplicate was added.

notAdded.candidate: Greater and lesser circles preserve word legibility
notAdded.reason: Visually useful scale comparison, but not selected for this small batch: comparison is more clearly demonstrated by the curated fulcrum, while the circles add less distinct reusable choreography. Actual closeup samples were inspected.

notAdded.candidate: Water separation, ground rise and creature emergence
notAdded.reason: Overview candidates overlap existing separation, terrain, formation and whale-composite principles; no additional cards justified from these samples.
